## Ontario Lease Change Snapshot

This looks like a **fixed-term Ontario residential tenancy** that started on **2025-09-01**. A rent increase on **2026-03-01** may be possible only if it follows Ontario rules, including proper notice and timing; the one-month deposit is usually treated as a **rent deposit**, not an extra fee.

## Tenant Checklist for Documents, Questions, and Reply

| Topic | What to keep or ask | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Lease paperwork | Signed lease, all addenda, renewal letters, move-in condition notes | Proves the agreed rent, term, and any special terms |
| Rent records | Receipts, e-transfers, bank statements, landlord messages | Shows what was paid and when |
| Deposit record | Proof of the one-month deposit and how the landlord described it | Helps confirm whether it was a lawful rent deposit |
| Rent increase notice | Copy of any written notice, date received, effective date | Lets you check whether notice and timing are proper |
| Building history | Ask whether the unit is rent-controlled and when it was first occupied for residential use | Helps determine whether annual guideline limits may apply |
| Repairs/issues | Photos, repair requests, response dates | Useful if the rent increase is being discussed alongside maintenance problems |

### Questions to ask the landlord
- Is this increase being treated as a formal Ontario rent increase notice?
- What is the current lawful rent, and what exact amount is being requested?
- When was the last rent increase, and what was the effective date?
- Is the unit subject to Ontario rent control based on first residential occupancy?
- Is the one-month deposit being held as a rent deposit, and will it be applied only to the last month of tenancy?
- Can you send the notice and supporting details in writing?

### Practical tenant checklist
- Keep everything in one folder: lease, notices, receipts, emails, texts, photos.
- Save screenshots of any messages with dates visible.
- Do not rely on verbal conversations alone.
- Compare the proposed increase date against the date of the last increase.
- If the notice seems improper, reply politely in writing and ask for clarification before paying more.
- If you need to challenge it later, your paper trail will matter more than phone calls.

### Polite written reply
Use a calm, non-accusatory tone:
- Confirm you received the message.
- Ask for the increase details in writing.
- State that you want to review the notice and lease terms.
- Do not admit the increase is valid if you are unsure.
- Keep the message short and professional.

## Sample Email Draft

Subject: Request for Written Details About Proposed Rent Increase

Hello [Landlord Name],

Thank you for your message about the proposed rent increase effective 2026-03-01.

I would appreciate it if you could send the increase details in writing, including the current lawful rent, the amount requested, the effective date, and the notice form or basis being relied on. I would also like to confirm how the one-month deposit is being held and whether the unit is subject to Ontario rent control.

I am reviewing the lease and my records, and I will respond once I have the written details.

Thank you,
[Tenant Name]

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Review LTB rules](https://tribunalsontario.ca/ltb/)
Action: [Button: Ontario rent guide](https://www.ontario.ca/page/renting-ontario-your-rights)

- Advocacy Centre for Tenants Ontario: https://www.acto.ca/
